title: Dejan's first alto and paying for it from Tea Garden tips
summary: Dejan recounts his father buying a silver horn and his brother a gold trumpet, and paying 325 for his own alto from tips.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: . . . that the good horn, take that good horn and play it in parade. Because black horns can't take that way. You see that horn you see me play in parade? That's my first horn. That's my very first alto. Well no, I take that back. I had a silver horn I kept for one week. My daddy bought me a silver horn and he bought my brother a gold trumpet. That didn't work. That didn't work. He said, when you start on that regular job at the Japanese tea garden, you get what kind of horn you want. I said, you get me the horn and I'll pay it for it. He said, when you can't pay it but I'll pay it for it. I said, okay. I paid 325 pounds for that horn and pay for that horn in three months and two weeks off my tips. That's right. Daddy said, well, you know I'm a pair for this. Don't you think you're going to make that money, you can pay for that horn? I said, yes, I'll pay for it. Now he paid cash for that silver horn. I kept it one week. That went right back where I see the other day. That'd be a gold horn. Buy my brother a gold trumpet and I got a silver one. What's that way? Boy, his brother could play them.
